title: Mental cruelty as a divorce ground - recent trends in judgments
p1: Can a marriage end even without physical violence? The answer may surprise many. Courts today are looking beyond visible injuries and examining the emotional impact of a relationship.
p2: A common belief is that mental cruelty means only extreme abuse. But recent judgments show that repeated humiliation, constant suspicion, unreasonable behaviour, and creating unbearable emotional stress can also become grounds for divorce. The key factor is not one isolated incident, but the overall effect on a spouse’s mental well-being.
p3: Courts have increasingly focused on whether the conduct has made continuing the marriage practically impossible. This does not mean every disagreement is cruelty. Ordinary conflicts are part of married life, but a pattern of harmful behaviour may cross the legal threshold. The takeaway: mental cruelty is judged from real-life circumstances, not just words written on paper.
conclusion: Do you think emotional suffering should receive the same legal attention as physical harm in divorce cases?
